title: I want to build a price tracker/predictor.
author: Obvious_Donkey_505
selftext:
​

Hi everyone, I know this might be new and maybe a little odd for some of you. 

I am M22, engaged in my family business of spices and dry fruits. We are a spice manufacturing company but let's say on a smaller scale and I want to scale this company in the next 5 years and to do that I want to integrate AI as much as possible.

Now here's my idea I want you all to help me validate: 

I want to take a jump and cumin trading in bulk (from current 300kgs/month to 1000kgs/month in the next 3 months). I don't want to go into the details of the commodity and margin but just for context,

Currently my margin (barring the fluctuations) is around ₹10-20/kg which will go down to ₹5-8/kg. The crucks is that the main earning is in fluctuations (going upto ₹50-100/kg). If you know how commodity market works. (I can tell more for better understanding if anyone asks about it). 

My idea is to build an AI tracker (backed by deepseek or groq). There are two parts to it, 

1. A python scraper which will collect daily prices from APMC. Also news related to cumin prices. 

The scraper will document daily (and historical, 5 years) prices in google sheets, feed the news to AI. The AI, based on all the information available — which is news, Current price and historical data + seasons will generate a confidence score and based on that score it should suggest me if I should hold the stock/buy new stock or dump it. 

Here's the roadmap of the project by my ChatGPT. **The question I want to ask you all is, is this project practical. Can anyone of you suggest something to make it better or more efficient?** 

***Proposed Roadmap***

I am thinking of building this in phases rather than trying to build a fully autonomous AI system from day one.

Phase 1 — Data Collection

\\- Use government APMC/AGMARKNET APIs to collect daily cumin prices from Unjha and major Rajasthan markets.

\\- Collect historical mandi prices (ideally 5+ years).

\\- Build a Python-based news scraper/RSS collector to identify news specifically related to cumin: arrivals, production, weather, exports, demand, etc.

\\- Manually enter supplier quotations into Google Sheets.

Phase 2 — Data Processing & Storage

\\- Store daily market prices, supplier quotations and relevant news in Google Sheets.

\\- Clean and standardize market names, dates, grades and price units.

\\- Remove duplicate records and identify missing or suspicious data.

\\- Build a historical database for seasonal and trend analysis.

Phase 3 — AI Analysis (Groq/DeepSeek API)

\\- Use an LLM to classify news as bullish, bearish or neutral.

\\- Identify recurring seasonal patterns from historical prices.

\\- Analyse current price movements against historical trends.

\\- Combine market data, news and supply/demand indicators to generate a market assessment.

Phase 4 — Forecasting & Backtesting

\\- Experiment with statistical and machine-learning models to forecast price direction over 7–14 days.

\\- Test predictions against historical data.

\\- Compare model performance with simple forecasting methods.

\\- Measure accuracy before allowing forecasts to influence actual buying decisions.

Phase 5 — Alerts & Decision Support

\\- Integrate Telegram for daily market reports and price alerts.

\\- Generate recommendations such as BUY, WAIT, HOLD or REDUCE STOCK.

\\- Include supporting evidence, expected risks and a confidence score with every recommendation.

Long-term objective: Build a system that continuously accumulates market intelligence, learns from historical price behaviour and helps me make better purchasing and inventory-holding decisions.

I don't necessarily intend to train an LLM from scratch. I am more interested in combining existing LLMs with a dedicated statistical/ML forecasting model and continuously growing our own commodity-specific dataset.

comments.author: tradematesHQ
comments.body: The scraper and historical data part is solid, but an AI confidence score on commodity prices is basically astrology with extra steps. APMC data is messy and lagged, so garbage in garbage out. Build the data pipeline first, skip the prediction layer until you trust the inputs.
